messages.subject: measurementInvariance Error
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm currently running some measurement invariance tests, and have run into a small roadblock.  The authors I am working with are interested in a second-order/hierarchical model, which fits relatively well (using cfa(), and the options: std.lv = TRUE, std.ov = TRUE, and orthogonal = TRUE).  This model has one overarching factor, and four sub-factors which load onto the items (each item only loads on one subfactor).

We are currently testing for invariance across gender, with the following syntax: measurementInvariance(model = model, data = data, std.lv = TRUE, std.ov = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE, group = "sex").

This approach works with the correlated CFA model (no overarching factor, without the orthogonal parameter), but when we apply it to the second-order factor, lavaan yields the following warning:

In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!

I thought this might be because a particular model might not have converged, but I reran the model with verbose = TRUE, and it appears each of the four models converged.  Is this function perhaps not designed for second-order CFAs?  Or am I doing something else wrong?

Any advice would be extremely appreciated!

Best,

Matt

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: measurementInvariance Error
parts:
Hi Matt,

What version of semTools are you using? Older versions had some difficulty with higher order factors. I'd recommend using the newest version (0.4-5) available from: https://github.com/simsem/semTools/wiki

Alex

messages.subject: Re: measurementInvariance Error
parts:
I've updated semTools to 0.4-5, but unfortunately it yields the same error.

For specifying the second-order model, is it acceptable to do so as (for example):

model <- '
overall =~ F1 + F2 + F3 + F4
F1 =~ Q1 + ... + Q8   # 8 items
F2 =~ Q9 + ... + Q16 # 8 items
F3 =~ Q17 + ... + Q21 # 4 items
F4 =~ Q22 + ... + Q24 # 3 items
`
measurementInvariance(model, data = data, std.lv = TRUE, std.ov = TRUE, orthogonal = TRUE, group = "Sex")

To check for measurement invariance across loadings, and:

measurementInvariance(model, data = data, orthogonal = TRUE, group = "Sex")

To check for measurement invariance across factor means?

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: measurementInvariance Error
parts:
Matt,

Sunthud is correct. I got confused between measurementInvariance and another function (which does work with higher order factors). In your case, I think you'd be best served using lavaan itself and the group.equal option. If you want to test the lower and higher order factors for invariance separately, you could always specify the higher order factor loadings as regression paths and use the "regressions" options for group.equal to test if the higher order factor loadings are equal across groups.

Alex
